verdicts.answerable_part: A formal study can define assignment units, exposure mappings, version-specific strategies, and identified estimands for a bounded class of policy interventions, but it cannot supply universal equivalence classes or minimum jurisdiction counts.
verdicts.design_sketch: For a specified staggered jurisdiction-level policy, define the counterfactual risk under explicit exposure mappings and treatment-version distributions, then derive which contrasts are identified as interference, version heterogeneity, and the number of jurisdictions vary. Use nonidentification results and asymptotic variance to determine which protocol failures change the estimand and which only reduce precision.
verdicts.priority_note: Run a narrowly scoped analytic study later; the catalog rating is defensible, but the problem is too heterogeneous for one general answer.

verdicts.answerable_part: A standards process can define decision-specific evidence requirements and dossier components, but no empirical study can identify a universal acceptable level of residual confounding or emulation adequacy.
verdicts.design_sketch: Elicit regulator and decision-maker judgments for scenarios varying clinical effect size, consequence of error, protocol fidelity, and sensitivity-analysis results. Estimate consensus thresholds and their between-reviewer reliability separately for each decision context rather than treating adequacy as one numerical estimand.
verdicts.priority_note: Do not run this early as a methods study; it is primarily a regulatory standards problem and requires institutional participation.

verdicts.answerable_part: A study can validate and standardize a candidate dashboard for longitudinal balance, support, weights, and artificial censoring, but it cannot make untestable assumptions empirically diagnosable or compel adoption.
verdicts.design_sketch: Use a Delphi process to select dashboard panels, then have independent reviewers apply the candidate dashboard to emulations varying follow-up length, treatment-history support, weight instability, and artificial censoring. Judge success by interrater reliability, omission detection, and whether each diagnostic is correctly mapped to the assumption it can assess.
verdicts.priority_note: The longitudinal diagnostic components merit early development, but the full high-priority dashboard should wait for a standards process.

verdicts.answerable_part: A corpus study can measure how often target trial emulation labels are accompanied by unsupported causal conclusions and can classify the assumptions actually addressed, but it cannot establish a universally correct ladder or change how readers interpret the label.
verdicts.design_sketch: Sample published target trial emulations and classify the strongest stated conclusion, the assumptions explicitly justified, and whether temporal alignment was implemented. Estimate the proportion whose causal claims exceed their documented assumptions, with blinded duplicate coding and interrater agreement.
verdicts.priority_note: This is a feasible early meta-research project, but it is a reporting problem rather than a target trial emulation methods problem.

verdicts.answerable_part: A simulation can determine the bias, coverage, and efficiency consequences of repeated participation, calendar-time heterogeneity, and alternative variance estimators under specified mechanisms, but it cannot establish that later eligibility is innocuous across all outcome models.
verdicts.design_sketch: Estimate a pooled 5-year risk difference from sequential nested trials while varying calendar trends, treatment-effect modification by trial start, repeated eligibility, and survival-dependent re-entry. Compare naive, person-clustered, and person-bootstrap inference on bias, 95% interval coverage, and effective efficiency relative to a single baseline trial.
verdicts.priority_note: Run this early because it is a clean, consequential simulation even though the catalog statement overstates how unsettled person-level dependence is.

verdicts.answerable_part: An analytic study can derive valid scalable variance for one fully specified estimator and nuisance-fitting regime, but it cannot provide a default covering arbitrary machine-learned nuisance models, sites, cloning schemes, and sequence expansions.
verdicts.design_sketch: For a cloned sequential-trial estimator of a 5-year per-protocol risk difference, derive an original-person clustered influence function that includes estimated censoring weights. Verify the formula against a person-level bootstrap under varying clone counts and trial participation, using coverage, computation time, and memory as performance measures.
verdicts.priority_note: This deserves high priority after the target estimator is fixed, but a general scalable default is too ambitious for a one-week study.

verdicts.answerable_part: A known structural data-generating mechanism can test whether distributional fidelity predicts causal fidelity for specified interventions, but it cannot validate counterfactual fidelity for generators trained only on real observational data.
verdicts.design_sketch: Generate longitudinal data with known sustained-strategy counterfactual risks, fit competing synthetic-data generators, and vary overlap, rare causal strata, and privacy strength. Compare marginal fidelity with intervention-response error, conditional-effect error, positivity preservation, and disclosure risk.
verdicts.priority_note: This is a useful causal-methods benchmark, but it should not run early in a target trial emulation program because the same problem arises in any causal use of synthetic data.

verdicts.answerable_part: A corpus audit can estimate artifact availability and practical rerunnability, but it cannot establish that a particular disclosure package is legally feasible or sufficient across proprietary data environments.
verdicts.design_sketch: Sample recent longitudinal emulations and estimate the proportion providing executable code, versioned phenotype definitions, protocol history, weight diagnostics, and simulated test data. Vary journal policy and data-access restrictions, and score whether an independent analyst can execute the pipeline and reproduce prespecified diagnostic outputs.
verdicts.priority_note: This is an inexpensive early corpus study with a clear result, although it measures reproducibility practice rather than estimator performance.

verdicts.answerable_part: A study can construct and assess equivalence classes for one treatment, indication, and era, but no empirical or consensus procedure can establish clinically defensible classes across treatments in general.
verdicts.design_sketch: For one indication, have a clinical panel define outcome-blind version classes across dose, route, formulation, combinations, and adherence, then compare alternative classifications for agreement, treatment-history support, and stability of a per-protocol risk contrast. Treat effect-estimate stability as a sensitivity result, not as evidence that a class is clinically correct.
verdicts.priority_note: Despite its high rating, this is a weak candidate for an early general study; begin with one clinically bounded consensus pilot.

verdicts.answerable_part: A simulation can compare outcome-blind selection rules and quantify sensitivity to grids and grace periods, but it cannot recover the clinically meaningful interval or grace period from treatment and observation processes alone.
verdicts.design_sketch: Estimate the 5-year risk difference under a sustained initiation strategy while varying treatment latency, visit intensity, within-interval event ordering, and true adherence behavior. Select grids using masked treatment and visit intensities, vary grace periods from 0 to 180 days, and compare methods on bias, interval coverage, ordering conflicts, and regret relative to the best prespecified specification.
verdicts.priority_note: Run this early because it offers a decisive comparison of prespecified procedures, while presenting any selected grid as a performance rule rather than a universal truth.

verdicts.answerable_part: A study can compare a prespecified sequence of negative controls, proxies, and validation information for one estimand and set of identification assumptions, but it cannot determine a generally correct way to combine methods whose assumptions conflict.
verdicts.design_sketch: For a sustained-treatment risk difference, simulate time-varying unmeasured confounding with proxies and negative controls of varying relevance and strength, then apply the same workflow to a published emulation with usable controls. Compare bias, coverage, instability, and the frequency with which each diagnostic correctly signals failure of its own assumptions.
verdicts.priority_note: The catalog priority is too high for this program; it is an important general unmeasured-confounding problem, but the emulation label adds little unless the study is explicitly longitudinal.

verdicts.answerable_part: An analytic study can derive a joint identification region for a fixed sustained-strategy estimand and a prespecified set of bias models, but no universal region exists without unverifiable bounds or priors for each violation and their dependence.
verdicts.design_sketch: Define the 5-year risk difference under a sustained strategy with bounded time-varying confounding, exposure misclassification, informative selection, and near-positivity violations. Optimize the causal contrast over the joint bias-parameter space, derive when marginal regions fail to combine, and use simulation to assess region coverage and the error from product approximations.
verdicts.priority_note: Do not run this early; it is theoretically important but assumption-heavy, and a useful first study must restrict both the estimand and the violation models sharply.

verdicts.answerable_part: A study can define and identify a mediated effect for one sustained strategy, mediator schedule, and intercurrent-event policy, but it cannot produce a universally mechanistic proportion mediated or solve the incompatible interpretations of natural and interventional effects.
verdicts.design_sketch: Define an interventional indirect effect on 2-year risk for two sustained strategies with a mediator measured at one prespecified time and artificial censoring at strategy deviation. Derive identification when mediator history predicts censoring, characterize violations of the mediational null, and verify the proposed estimator by simulation under known counterfactual risks.
verdicts.priority_note: This is a genuine core problem, but the full statement is too broad; prioritize a one-mediator identification result before attempting repeated mediators or sequential trials.

verdicts.answerable_part: A corpus study can estimate an empirical discrepancy distribution for aligned trial-emulation pairs within a bounded domain, but it cannot identify how much of each discrepancy is emulation bias rather than effect modification, population differences, or estimand mismatch.
verdicts.design_sketch: Assemble paired randomized trials and emulations, align each treatment contrast, follow-up horizon, outcome scale, and target population, then estimate the distribution of log-effect discrepancies. Vary protocol-match quality and data source, and evaluate heterogeneity and out-of-sample calibration of the resulting discrepancy prior rather than treating each difference as identified bias.
verdicts.priority_note: This deserves early scoping but not immediate execution; it is central to benchmarking, yet credible pairing and estimand alignment will take longer than a week.
